grammar_concept.title: First Conditional: if + Present Simple, will + base verb
grammar_concept.rule: Use the First Conditional to talk about real, possible situations in the future and their likely result: "If" + Present Simple, "will" + base verb.
grammar_concept.simple_explanation: This is for things that could really happen — not imaginary or impossible situations, just realistic "if this happens, then this will happen" predictions.
grammar_concept.example: If it rains, we will stay home. If you study hard, you'll pass the exam.
grammar_concept.example_translation: Se chover, ficamos em casa. Se estudares muito, vais passar no exame.
grammar_concept.common_mistake_pt: Falantes de português tendem a usar "will" nas duas partes da frase, porque em português o futuro pode aparecer nas duas orações: dizem "If it will rain, we will stay home" em vez de "If it rains, we will stay home" — a parte depois de "if" nunca leva "will" no First Conditional, mesmo falando do futuro.
grammar_concept.correction: A parte com "if" usa sempre Present Simple (rains, study, is), nunca "will". Só a segunda parte (o resultado) leva "will" + verbo base. "If" + will é um erro muito comum e muito notado por nativos.
grammar_concept.real_world_example: Num email de trabalho: "If you send the report by Friday, I will review it over the weekend."

vocabulary.definition_en: except if; used to introduce a condition that prevents something
example_sentences: We won't go unless the weather improves.

vocabulary.definition_en: used to talk about doing something as a precaution
example_sentences: Take an umbrella in case it rains.
I'll call you as soon as I arrive.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: If she ___ (have) time, she will call you tomorrow.
exercises.explanation: A parte depois de "if" usa Present Simple ("has"), nunca "will".
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Usar "will have" depois de "if" é o erro mais comum nesta estrutura.

correct_answer: If it rains, we will stay home.
distractors: If it will rain, we will stay home.
If it rains, we stay home will.
If it will rains, we will stay home.
exercises.explanation: Só a parte do resultado (depois da vírgula) leva "will".
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Colocar "will" na parte do "if" é o erro clássico de falantes de português nesta estrutura.

correct_answer: except if; used to introduce a condition that prevents something
exercises.explanation: "Unless" é essencialmente "if not" — introduz uma exceção que impede algo.

exercises.prompt: Listen to the audio. What will happen if the team wins?
correct_answer: they will celebrate at a restaurant
exercises.explanation: No áudio, ouve-se: "If the team wins tonight, we will celebrate at a restaurant afterwards."
exercises.transcript: If the team wins tonight, we will celebrate at a restaurant afterwards.

exercises.prompt: Read the text: "If you arrive before 9am, you will get a free coffee. Unless you have a reservation, you might have to wait for a table." What happens if you arrive before 9am?
correct_answer: you will get a free coffee
distractors: you have to wait for a table
exercises.explanation: O texto indica diretamente: "you will get a free coffee".

exercises.prompt: Translate to English: "Se acabares o trabalho cedo, podemos ir jantar fora."
correct_answer: If you finish work early, we can go out for dinner.
exercises.explanation: "Se acabares" (futuro em PT) corresponde a Present Simple em inglês ("if you finish"), não a "will finish".
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Traduzir diretamente o futuro do português para "will" na parte do "if" é o erro mais comum.

steps.content: "Will" is almost always contracted and reduced in natural speech: "I will" → "I'll" /aɪl/, "we will" → "we'll" /wiːl/ — native speakers rarely say the full "will" in casual conversation.

steps.prompt: Talk about 3 real plans using "If... , I will..." (e.g. weather, weekend, work).
Write 5 sentences about realistic future possibilities using the First Conditional.
